focus: New chamber-graph layout generator and gen step: passage routing, divider placement, fog behaviour, save data
diffSource: since build 21 (2026-10-07T18:40:56Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Rubble dividers can strand a party that has no pawn able to mine
findings.detail: Every connection gets a divider and about 45% of them are rubble (`Rand.Chance(0.55f)` picks Door, otherwise Rubble). Rubble is a Mineable and is the only way past that passage. A tree edge can be the only route to the rest of the dungeon. If no pawn in the party can do Mining work, the party cannot get past it. That may be intended. If it isn't, force the first divider out of the entrance chamber (depth 0 to 1) to be a Door, or note the requirement on the entry dialog.

findings.title: Door access for animals only applies to dungeons created from now on
findings.detail: `doorsAlwaysOpenForPlayerPawns` is set only when a new site is created in DungeonEntry. It is saved on MapParent, so new saves keep it. A site that already existed (made in build 21 or earlier, or reused on re-entry through some other path) lacks the flag. Its map has no doors anyway, because the old placeholder step made none. If a site can be reused and its map regenerated, set the flag in the same place that sets `layoutSeed` rather than only at creation. Check that.

findings.title: Old saves load with a null `site.layout`
findings.detail: `Scribe_Deep.Look(ref layout, "layout")` leaves `layout` null for sites saved before this build. The generator code is fine, because `Scribe_Collections` null-guards the lists. The phase 4 code that reads `site.layout` must null-check it. A site's map that was already generated keeps its old placeholder layout and has no chamber data.

findings.title: Map size depends on the current MaxLevel setting
findings.detail: `MapSizeFor` scales by `(level-1)/(max-1)`, and `max` falls back to the live setting. The comment says the same dungeon is the same size for every party. That holds only while `maxLevel` is unchanged. Changing the setting resizes the dungeon at that level. This is harmless because generation happens once per entry, but the comment overstates it.

findings.title: Unconditional Log.Message on every map generation
findings.detail: The gen step logs one info line per dungeon entry. That is fine while developing. Drop it or gate it behind a dev-mode check before release so players' logs stay quiet.

findings.title: A layout with a single chamber is possible
findings.detail: If every route is refused, all other chambers are dropped and only chamber 0 remains: one room, no dividers, just the exit. It is very unlikely at these map sizes, and it is handled without exceptions (`Compile` and the gen step both cope with an empty dividers list). Phase 4 should not assume at least two chambers.

findings.title: Rubble is the only way through some passages and has no yield, so a party that can't mine is stuck
findings.detail: Rubble-divided passages can only be opened by mining. A party with no pick or no one able to mine cannot progress, and explosives or fire can also open them. If the layout generator can seal a branch behind rubble alone, make sure a door or an alternate route always exists, or accept this as design. I did not read the generator code, which another reviewer has, so I could not confirm whether it guarantees this.

findings.title: TUBAD_DungeonRubble omits building.isNaturalRock, so it is a normal building to the game
findings.detail: This is probably intended, since it keeps it out of the rock-only code paths such as smoothing and the stone chunk lists. The side effect is that `ListerBuildings` tracks it as a non-colonist building. It is also destroyed through `Building.Destroy`'s non-rock path, which may leave rubble filth beyond what `filthLeaving` implies. I judge this harmless.
